notes: Classic hunt (101k fractions): 21 pi identities, 11 up to shift/scaling, 0 control hits. Fast (exponential) hits sit at the convergence boundary: a(n)=a1 n + a0 with a1^2 + 4 b2 small (2n+1 | n^2 and the 3n | -2n^2 family, where 9 - 8 = 1). Slow (power-law) hits are Euler-type: constant a with b(n) = 4n^2 + ... . Round 1 probes both regimes further and tries one degree up.

families.name: r1 boundary: a1 = 4..7, b2 near -a1^2/4
families.rationale: If the 3n | -2n^2 pattern (a1^2 + 4 b2 = 1) generalises, a1 = 4..7 with b2 in [-12,-3] should contain new exponential identities.

families.name: r1 Euler-type: constant a, b = c n^2 + ...
families.rationale: Euler's pi+3 = 6 + 1/(6 + 9/(6 + ...)) and the 8 | 4n^2-1 hit suggest more constant-a fractions with larger a and b2 a perfect square.

families.name: r1 one degree up: quadratic a, quartic b with b(0) = 0
families.rationale: Formulas like Apery's use a(n) quadratic and b(n) = -n^4-type; test whether pi has fast fractions there.
